19.0.0.en: The two angels, who were the two angels present at the meeting with Abraham, arrived at Sodom and entered by the gate of the city, where there is usually a square in which the judges and the people sit. It was evening and most of the people of the city had gone off to their houses, so Lot hurried to them to host them, and bowed down in respect and welcome to them.

19.1.0.en: Lot offered them his love by hosting them in his house, so that they might wash their feet, eat and rest, and then continue their journey the next day. But they refused Lot's invitation and wanted to spend the night in the square, as a declaration of their rejection of the city's evils and of not mixing with them, and an implicit rebuke to Lot for accepting to live among the wicked.

19.2.0.en: Lot held on to them and repeated his invitation many times until they accepted the invitation and went to his house, where he offered them unleavened bread, that is, bread without leaven, which can be made quickly, and they ate at his house.

19.3.0.en: The men of Sodom gathered around Lot's house and asked him to give them the two men, his guests, so that they might sin with them, because this whole city had fallen into the sin of homosexual perversion, so that this sin was called the Sodomite sin.

19.4.0.en: When the cries of the men of Sodom rose, demanding the guests, Lot went out to them and begged them not to do evil to these two guests.

19.5.0.en: The cries of the men of Sodom increased, so Lot showed his readiness to offer these wicked men his two virgin daughters to sin with them instead of the guests, and perhaps he wanted by this to shame them so that they would leave and let him be. But in any case he erred by this wicked offer, and perhaps he said it because he was influenced by living among the wicked, so that he accepted, if only in intention, to offer his two daughters for fornication.

19.6.0.en: The men of Sodom rejected Lot's offer of his two daughters, insisting on taking the two men, because they were attached to homosexual perversion to a degree beyond fornication with women, so they moved toward Lot's house to break it down and rape the two men.

19.7.0.en: The two men, that is, the two angels, hurried, opened the door, pulled Lot into the house and shut the door before the men reached him.

19.8.0.en: The two angels struck the men of Sodom with blindness, so they were alarmed and stumbled against one another. Strangely, they did not repent of their evil after this calamity, the blindness that befell them, and they kept searching for the door to burst into the house, blind as they were, to rape the two men, but they were unable to reach the door and, blinded, wandered away from it.

19.8.1.en: Do not be lenient with sin, lest you grow accustomed to it and cling to it and even justify it, and so blind your heart to God and the truth. Hasten to repentance so that you may discover your sin, trust that by God's power you can overcome it, and partake of the Holy Mysteries, so that you taste the sweetness of God and shelter by His power from your evils.

19.9.0.en: The two angels declared to Lot that God would destroy Sodom and Gomorrah and all the cities of the plain because of their immersion in evil, and said to him, bring out whomever you have in the city, whether those who live in your house, the believers in God, that is, his wife and his two virgin daughters, and also his married daughters with their husbands, who are called Lot's sons-in-law. Although his sons-in-law were from the people of Sodom, God was ready to save them if they believed in Him and showed it by going out with Lot.

19.10.0.en: The angels' speech was at night, so Lot hurried to warn his sons-in-law and his daughters so that they would prepare to leave Sodom, but they did not believe his words about the destruction of the city and considered them jesting and not true. Sadly, Lot's married daughters lost their faith in God and their trust in their father's words and were carried along after their husbands' words, so they perished with them and with the rest of the people of Sodom.

19.11.0.en: The night passed with his sons-in-law and his daughters insisting on not obeying God's word, so the two angels intervened, warned Lot of the nearness of the city's destruction and asked him to hurry out, he and his wife and his two virgin daughters.

19.12.0.en: Lot kept lingering over leaving because of his attachment to his daughters and sons-in-law and his longing that they obey so as to be saved, and perhaps he was also thinking of his possessions, all of which he would leave behind in Sodom. So the two angels had to seize him and his wife and his two daughters and pull them out of the city that was about to burn.

19.13.0.en: When the angel brought Lot and those with him out, one of the two angels, the leading one, commanded him not to look back, he and those with him, that is, to cut off every attachment to the material things he had left in Sodom, since all had been defiled by evil, and to flee away from the city with all speed, leaving all the plain (the Jordan plain), which means the whole region of evil, and to go to the mountain, where escape lies in height and spiritual elevation.

19.14.0.en: Lot asked leave of the angel who was speaking to him that He spare the small city which lies at the edge of the plain of the Jordan, east of the Dead Sea, and which was called Bela, so that he might flee to it and not live in the mountain, lest wild beasts attack him or he suffer harm in this wilderness.

19.14.1.en: It was weakness of faith in Lot to fear living in the mountain although it was God who commanded him to, and to ask to live in a city which truly lies at the edge of this evil region but could have been defiled, if only partly. I wish you would obey God however difficult His commands seem in your eyes, and not rely on your reason against God's commandments, for He knows your good better than you ... only believe in Him and you will find your salvation and rest.

19.15.0.en: I have favored you also concerning this thing: I have honored you and agreed to your request.

19.15.1.en: God agreed to Lot's intercession for this small city and did not destroy it for his sake, and this is clear proof for the second time of the importance of intercession, after Abraham's intercession for Sodom and Gomorrah.

19.16.0.en: The angel asked Lot to hurry toward Zoar so that God might carry out His word by burning Sodom and all around it, and he called the city of Bela by the name Zoar because it is small, as Lot said. Here God's great care for His children appears, that He cannot do any harm to the wicked that could touch His children, even a little. It is fitting here to compare Abraham and Lot, and the following appears:

19.16.2.en: 1- He lived in the wilderness. | 1- He lived in the fertile city.

19.16.3.en: 2- He let God choose for him. | 2- He chose for himself.

19.16.4.en: 3- He saved Lot by God's power. | 3- He was weak, so he was taken captive by Chedorlaomer.

19.16.5.en: 4- He took nothing of the spoils after his victory | 4- He was absorbed in the pleasures of Sodom.

19.16.7.en: 5- God and two angels visited him. | 5- Only two angels visited him.

19.16.8.en: 6- God and the two angels welcomed entering his place. | 6- The two angels refused to enter, and after urging they entered his house.

19.16.9.en: 7- God promised him blessed offspring. | 7- The two angels warned him of the destruction of the city.

19.16.10.en: 8- He entered into dialogue with God. | 8- His speech with the two angels was brief.

19.16.11.en: 9- He believed in God. | 9- He believed the words of the two angels but obeyed with difficulty, so they pulled him out of the city.

19.16.12.en: 10- He increased with the birth of Isaac, and his possessions were many. | 10- He lost his wife, his married daughters and all his possessions.

19.16.13.en: 11- He lived in the wilderness and enjoyed many appearances of God. | 11- He refused to live in the mountain and asked

19.16.14.en: 12- He interceded for the wicked, that they might repent, that is, that Sodom be rescued. | to live in Zoar (Bela). 12- He interceded for Zoar so that it would not be destroyed for

19.16.15.en: 13- God kept him because of his faith and obedience. | his own personal benefit.

19.16.16.en: 13- God kept him because of Abraham's intercession.

19.17.s.en: (3) The destruction of Sodom and Lot's wife

19.17.0.en: God's mercies appear in His waiting for Lot's entry into the city of Zoar at the beginning of the day at sunrise, and immediately God rained fire and brimstone from heaven on Sodom and Gomorrah and all the cities of the plain, and everything in them burned, human beings, animals, plants and all that existed. The following appears from this:

19.17.1.en: 1- God's long-suffering and His mercies toward those who believe in Him, whereas His wrath on the wicked and the obstinate is very heavy.

19.17.2.en: 2- The Holy Trinity appears in (v. 24): "The Lord (the Son ...) rained ... from the Lord (the Father)."

19.18.0.en: Lot's wife did not obey God's word and looked back at Sodom, which had begun to burn, either from her attachment to her daughters or her possessions, so she became a pillar of salt, that is, she became a memorial for the soul that does not obey God. For after God had rescued her, her heart was still attached to wicked Sodom and what was in it, so she perished at once.

19.18.1.en: I wish you would look to your goal, who is God, at the beginning of each day, and put away your former sins of which you have repented, for remembering evil makes you fall into it again. Be obedient to God even if His word is against your material desires or your feelings, and so be rescued from the wicked world.

19.19.0.en: Abraham had been occupied with his speaking with God to save the city of Sodom, that perhaps the wicked in it would repent, and also to save Lot and his family, and perhaps he was occupied with this all night. So he rose early and walked on the road leading to Sodom, on which he had walked with God the day before.

19.20.0.en: Abraham looked toward Sodom and found the smoke of its fire rising toward heaven, and he grieved over its destruction. God did not forbid him to look at Sodom because he sought its salvation and return to God, whereas He forbade Lot and his family to look at Sodom, to stop their attachment to material things and to human feelings toward the defiled city and those in it, even if they were his daughters.

19.21.0.en: God looked at Abraham's righteousness and intercession and rescued Lot and those with him from destruction, for because of the righteous man God has mercy on those around him, as God blessed the house of Potiphar for Joseph's sake.

19.22.s.en: (4) The sin of Lot's two daughters with their father

19.22.0.en: Lot relied on his own thinking and chose to live in Zoar for fear of living in the mountain, but then he became afraid of living in Zoar, either because of the presence of wicked people in it or because of his lack of prompt obedience to God in living in the mountain, so he left Zoar and lived in a cave in the mountain.

19.22.1.en: Let your obedience to God's commandments be swift, for it is the shortest way to rest and reassurance. Material things or reason cannot give you peace, and the only source of it is God and obedience to His commandments.

19.23.0.en: The fear that was in Lot's heart was also in the heart of his two daughters, for they worried that there were no men to marry them, although there were tribes spread through the desert, but it was an anxiety they had acquired from Sodom through their mixing with the wicked in it.

19.24.0.en: The two daughters thought of a way to bear offspring, which was to lie with the only man before them, their father, but he would refuse, so they thought of making him drink wine until he lost his discernment, so that they might lie with him, and they actually carried out the idea. From this we understand that Lot had been defiled by his association with the Sodomites and loved wine, so that he accepted that his daughters prepare wine for him and drank much of it until he was drunk and lost his discernment, and moved in a lustful way toward his daughters; so the elder approached him and lay with him while he did not discern that she was his daughter or that he was lying with a female, and perhaps he thought himself in a dream ... and the same was repeated the next day, and the younger lay with him. However much the commentators try to find an excuse for these two daughters in their attempt to preserve the offspring, their error is great, for this is plain fornication and the use of a means, which is wine, to make their father lose the ability to discern so that he does what he does not want without awareness. As for Lot's sin, it is his accepting to drink much wine until he became without will or awareness, so his two daughters exploited this weakness of his before the love of wine.

19.25.0.en: It seems that the two daughters' lying with their father was not merely two consecutive nights but perhaps lasted for about a month or two until they conceived by their father, and this means Lot's immersion in the love of wine.

19.26.0.en: The elder daughter bore a son whom she called "Moab," that is, from the father, because she bore him by her father, while the younger called her son "Ben-ammi," that is, son of my people, ascribing him to her people and not her father. In any case, two peoples hostile to the people of God, the Jews, came out of them. Moab and the sons of Ammon lived east of the Jordan River, worshipped idols and lived in evil far from God.

19.26.1.en: Thus the story of righteous Lot ends with a sad event, the begetting of evil, because he loved the world and material things and was defiled by them and lost much of his purity, and likewise his family departed from God and his seed walked in the way of evil. Abraham in Gerar

20.0.0.en: Abraham lived more than 20 years at the oaks of Mamre west of the Jordan River, and then moved to Gerar, which lies in the south of Palestine about five miles from Gaza, between Kadesh and Shur, which lie in the south of Palestine and were discussed before. Perhaps the reason for his moving was a search for fertile pastures for his flocks or a famine in the region where he lived (map 6).

20.1.0.en: Abimelech, which means my father is king, was a title of the kings of Gerar like the title Pharaoh for the kings of Egypt.

20.1.1.en: Abraham, great in faith, fell this time also in weakness of faith when he feared for himself from the people of Gerar and their king, lest they take his wife Sarah for her beauty and kill him. He repeated the sin of lying and said she was his sister, relying on the fact that she was his sister from his father and not his full sister. But the intention here was a lie, as we said, to protect himself from the possibility that the people of Gerar would kill him.

20.1.2.en: When Abimelech learned that Sarah was Abraham's sister and saw her beauty, he was dazzled by it although she was approaching ninety years, so he sent and took her to his palace to be his wife. Sadly Abraham did not speak but let them take her because of his fear of them, forgetting God's appearances and His promise that she would bear, after some months, the son of promise, Isaac.

20.1.3.en: Accept detachment in your life, and even afflictions, for they protect you from many sins you do not know, and ask for God's help and it will suffice you and support you. And do not move in your life except after prayer and asking God's guidance, and so you will live reassured and pure.

20.2.0.en: God appeared to Abimelech in a dream by night, and it seems that He had struck him with a disease that made him unable to approach Sarah and fearful of death, and God told him that he would die because of his taking Abraham's wife by force.

20.3.0.en: Abimelech answered God that he had not approached Sarah, but in lowliness begged Him not to destroy him and his people, because he did not know that she was married, indeed Abraham had said she was his sister and she had said he was her brother. He therefore did not intend to do any evil and consequently did not deserve to be destroyed, he and all his people, because of his sin, for he had taken her to marry her with a pure heart.

20.4.0.en: God accepted Abimelech's plea and even said to him, because I know the purity of your heart in this matter, I kept you from erring in marrying Sarah, and perhaps that was by the sudden illness that God allowed Abimelech in this night, so that he was occupied with his illness, and it also afflicted his wife and maidservants with a disease that prevented them from bearing; it may have been pains and inability to give birth, as appears from (v. 18).

20.5.0.en: God describes Abraham as a prophet, that is, a great devout man near to God, so as to make Abimelech afraid to approach Sarah; indeed He asked Abimelech to beg Abraham to pray for him so that God would remove the diseases from them, and at the same time threatened Abimelech with death if he did not obey, although he had not yet erred, but to keep him away from error.

20.6.0.en: Abimelech feared God, who had appeared to him in a dream of the night, so when he woke early he hurried to gather his servants who helped him in leading the people and told them what he had heard from God. They were assured of it because all the women about to give birth suffered from inability to give birth, which increased their fear of God and their belief in the king's words.

20.7.0.en: Abimelech summoned Abraham and reproached him for his lie in saying that Sarah was his sister, which exposed the king and the kingdom to a great danger, namely marrying a married woman and angering God so that He would take vengeance on them. The king asked him what had made him do this great deed. God allowed Abimelech to reproach and rebuke Abraham, the man of faith, so that he would be humbled and repent and not think himself better than others because of his faith.

20.7.1.en: Accept the voice of God on the tongue of all around you, even if it is your child or any person who seems less than you, for you need to learn from every person to complete your repentance and spiritual striving, and by this you grow spiritually and the devil cannot overcome you.

20.8.0.en: Abraham did not apologize for his error but sadly offered unsound justifications, which are:

20.8.1.en: 1- His feeling that the people of Gerar had no fear of God, perhaps thinking them like the people of Sodom, so that they would kill him in order to take his wife by force. By this he fell into judging others, indeed into a false accusation, because in truth they had the fear of God, as evidenced by the obedience of Abimelech and the whole kingdom to the word of God who appeared to him in the dream.

20.8.2.en: 2- That Sarah was his sister from his father and not his full sister, and he had agreed with her to hide that she was his wife in any strange place they went to, so that no one would harm him. The truth is that this is a lie, since it hides his marriage to her and exposes her to a strange man's lying with her, so she errs and makes the one who lies with her err ... This is a wicked agreement on sin and is not acceptable, for a sound end does not justify a wrong means.

20.9.0.en: The fear of God was in Abimelech's heart, and it made him not only refrain from touching Sarah but also appeared in his treatment of Abraham, and this appears in the following:

20.9.1.en: 1- He reproached him for not declaring that Sarah was his wife, as mentioned before, for he wants to live pure and not take anyone's wife by force.

20.9.2.en: 2- He returned to him Sarah his wife.

20.9.3.en: 3- He honored him by giving him gifts of sheep and oxen.

20.9.4.en: 4- He also gave him menservants and maidservants.

20.9.5.en: 5- He welcomed him to live in the land of his kingdom in any place he wished.

20.10.0.en: A thousand pieces of silver: that is, a thousand shekels, and the shekel equals approximately 15 grams.

20.10.1.en: A covering of the eyes: honor and restoration of reputation.

20.10.2.en: You are vindicated: nothing harmed you, but you received compensation and a sufficient apology.

20.10.3.en: 6- He gave Abraham also a thousand pieces of silver, a valuable gift at that time by comparison with what Sarah or any of the people around them had, as an apology and restoration of honor, that she was exposed to being a wife, or was nominally called the wife of Abimelech for a short time, until God showed him that she was Abraham's wife.

20.10.4.en: Abimelech's great generosity and liberality are to be noted, as well as the delicacy of his feelings in his apology to Abraham and his offering him these gifts after learning that Sarah was his wife, and not as a bridal gift as in the case of Pharaoh.

20.10.5.en: Be generous in your dealings with others as long as you are able, for your generosity shows your love, especially if you have wronged another or another has felt distress for any reason, for your gifts and your care make his heart rejoice and restore his peace.

20.11.0.en: Had closed up every womb: He made the pregnant women who were about to give birth unable to do so despite their pains, or caused the fetuses to fall from the wombs of their pregnant mothers so that the term was not completed in their bellies, that is, He closed the womb from completing its work of maturing the fetuses.

20.11.1.en: After this evident love and generosity of Abimelech, God covered for Abraham and showed him to be a prophet and a man of blessing, and made him pray for the healing of the wife and the maidservants of Abimelech, so God healed them and they regained their ability to conceive and give birth.
